Title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via Unsanitized href in UrlField
Analysis:
The `UrlField` component parses a record's database value (untrusted user input) and directly renders it as the `href` attribute of a material-ui `Link` component without sanitizing the protocol/scheme. If a record contains a URL with a `javascript:` scheme, clicking the link executes arbitrary JS in the user's browser, leading to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS).

Conceptual Payload:
An admin accesses a datagrid list or a show page containing:
`<UrlField source="website" />`
Where the record's website field has the value:
`javascript:alert(document.domain)`

When the user clicks on the link, the browser executes the JavaScript payload.

Title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via Unsanitized href in FileField
Analysis:
The `FileField` component retrieves the file source URI/URL (untrusted user input) from the record context and sets it directly as the `href` attribute of an anchor (`Link`) tag. This value is never sanitized, validated, or restricted to safe protocols (e.g. http/https). This allows an attacker to supply a URI using the `javascript:` protocol. If a victim clicks on the file download link, the javascript URI is evaluated and executed in the context of the user's browser, leading to DOM-based XSS.

Conceptual Payload:
A record is loaded into the `FileField` with a source property containing:
`javascript:alert(document.cookie)`

When the victim clicks the link, the payload executes.

Title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via Unsanitized Array Item href in FileField
Analysis:
The `FileField` component parses an array of files, reads the `src` property of each file object, and binds it directly to the `href` attribute of the rendered `Link` element without protocol/scheme sanitization. This allows an attacker to inject `javascript:` URLs into individual array elements of a file list, leading to DOM-based XSS when clicked.

Conceptual Payload:
A record is loaded with a source property containing:
`[ { "title": "malicious_file.pdf", "src": "javascript:alert(1)" } ]`

When the user clicks the rendered list item, the browser evaluates `javascript:alert(1)`.
